questions.question: Explain the nature and characteristics of management in detail.
questions.solution_html:
• Nature and Characteristics of Management
  • Management is the process of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling
  • resources to achieve organisational objectives efficiently and effectively.
  • Characteristics
  • • Goal-oriented
  • • Universal process
  • • Continuous process
  • • Group activity
  • • Dynamic function
  • • Intangible force
  • • Multidisciplinary
  • • Decision-making process

questions.question: Discuss in detail the concept of delegation of authority.
questions.solution_html:
• Delegation of Authority
  • Delegation means assigning responsibility and authority to subordinates for performing
  • specific tasks.
  • Elements
  • • Assignment of duties
  • • Granting of authority
  • • Creation of accountability
  • Importance
  • • Reduces workload of managers
  • • Develops employee skills
  • • Ensures quick decision-making
  • • Improves efficiency

  • development and placement of employees.
  • Characteristics
  • • Human resource function
  • • Continuous process
  • • Concerned with right person for right job
  • • Includes training and development
  • • Essential at all levels

questions.question: Define organising and explain the characteristics and importance of / organising.
questions.solution_html:
• Organising
  • Organising is the process of identifying and grouping activities, assigning duties, delegating
  • authority, and establishing relationships among employees to achieve organisational
  • objectives effectively.
  • Characteristics of Organising
  • • Division of work into manageable activities
  • • Coordination among different departments and individuals
  • • Establishment of authority and responsibility relationships
  • • Delegation of authority to subordinates
  • • Formation of a clear organisational structure
  • • Achievement-oriented process
  • • Continuous and dynamic process
  • • Facilitates cooperation among employees
  • • Defines reporting relationships
  • • Ensures optimum utilisation of resources
  • Importance of Organising
  • • Facilitates achievement of organisational objectives
  • • Promotes specialization and efficiency
  • • Avoids duplication of work
  • • Clarifies authority and responsibility
  • • Ensures effective coordination
  • • Helps in optimum use of resources
  • • Improves communication within the organisation
  • • Encourages teamwork and cooperation
  • • Facilitates effective control and supervision
  • • Enables adaptation to changes
  • • Assists in employee development
  • • Enhances productivity and profitability

questions.question: Discuss the concept of motivation and analyse McGregor’s Theory of / Motivation.
questions.solution_html:
• Motivation: Motivation is the process of stimulating people to act in order to achieve
  • organisational and personal goals. It is an internal force that encourages employees to
  • perform better and achieve desired objectives.
  • Features of Motivation
  • • Psychological and continuous process
  • • Goal-oriented activity
  • • Influences human behaviour
  • • Improves efficiency and productivity
  • • Can be financial and non-financial
  • • Helps satisfy employee needs
  • Importance of Motivation
  • • Increases employee performance
  • • Improves morale and job satisfaction
  • • Reduces absenteeism and labour turnover
  • • Promotes teamwork and cooperation
  • • Enhances organisational productivity
  • • Encourages innovation and creativity
  • McGregor’s Theory of Motivation
  • Douglas McGregor developed two assumptions about human behaviour
questions.final_answer: Douglas McGregor developed two assumptions about human behaviour
